prompt:
Image 1 is the club crest. Images 2 to 5 are photographs of this athlete.

A clean product photograph of a complete Pickleball kit, laid out FLAT and neatly
arranged on a plain light grey surface, photographed from directly above.

EXACTLY ONE of each of these, in the frame, fully visible and not overlapping. A missing
item makes the plate unusable because the poses read the wardrobe from it — and a DUPLICATE
is just as bad, because two shirts leave the poses to choose which one is the kit:
- the shirt, laid flat and face up
- the shorts below it
- BOTH socks, laid out straight
- EXACTLY TWO SHOES IN THE WHOLE FRAME, never two pairs: ONE shoe seen from directly
  above, and the OTHER shoe of that same pair turned onto its side so its full profile
  and its outsole are visible. Two shoes, two views, so nothing about the footwear has
  to be guessed at when the poses are drawn from this plate.
- the ball or implement of Pickleball

THE KIT — these are settled decisions, not suggestions. Do not substitute anything.
- shirt: A COPPER short-sleeved athletic T-SHIRT exactly as photo2.png shows it: a plain crew neck, RAGLAN sleeve seams running from the neck to the underarm, and the body plain copper all over — there is NO contrasting shoulder seam colour, no stripe and no trim of any other colour, whatever the sport default says. The club badge sits SMALL ON THE LEFT CHEST, about a palm across: the copperline-kingfishers mark exactly as the crest artwork draws it — an upright rounded PATCH with its top two corners clipped, in pale cream, carrying the kingfisher diving head-first straight down with its wings swept back into a dart and its dagger beak at the bottom, in copper. It is the ONLY mark on the shirt. NO maker's logo, NO club name, NO player name, NO number and no lettering of any kind. The BACK of the shirt is not visible in any photograph; the DECISION is that it stays PLAIN COPPER: no number, no name, no badge and no lettering across the shoulders or anywhere on it. Pickleball does not number a shirt, and a number across his back would be a mark this shirt does not have.
- shorts: PLAIN COPPER athletic SHORTS exactly as photo2.png and photo3.png show them: the same copper as the shirt, reaching to just above the knee, with a plain flat elasticated waistband, a soft loose cut and no stripe, no piping and no side panel. NO maker's logo, no number and no lettering on them. (art:spec:verify kept reporting a white swoosh on the lower left leg after one was edited out; a 4x crop of photo2.png shows plain unbroken copper from the waistband to the hem. §33: the crop outranks the judge, and this line is not to be reverted on another verifier run.)
- socks: NO PHOTOGRAPH SHOWS HIS FEET — photo2.png and photo3.png both stop above the ankle. The DECISION is PLAIN WHITE ANKLE SOCKS, sitting just above the shoe collar, with no stripe and no maker's mark. The same pair in every frame.
- footwear: NO PHOTOGRAPH SHOWS HIS FEET, so this is a DECISION and not a reading: PLAIN WHITE COURT SHOES with pale grey side panels and white laces, a flat non-marking court sole and a slightly cushioned midsole — an ordinary comfortable club-player's shoe, not a racing flat and not a fashion sneaker. Completely PLAIN and UNBRANDED: no stripes device, no swoosh, no maker's mark and no lettering on the upper or the sole. The same pair in every frame.
- equipment: A PICKLEBALL PADDLE and a BALL, both plain. The paddle has a flat rounded rectangular face in light beige with a BLACK edge guard around it and a BLACK wrapped handle — the face is COMPLETELY BLANK, with no graphic, no swirl, no logo, no model name and no lettering on either side of it. NO BALL appears in any photograph; the DECISION is that where a pose needs one it is a plain YELLOW perforated plastic pickleball with round holes, unbranded, and it appears nowhere else. In photo3.png there are also plain unbranded bags and water bottles on the court beside him; the DECISION for the poses is that he carries the PADDLE and, where the action needs it, the BALL — and nothing else: no bag, no bottle, no towel.
- Where an item above is described from the athlete's own photographs, any manufacturer's
  logo it genuinely carries stays on it — that is their real clothing.
- The club crest sits SMALL ON THE LEFT CHEST, about a palm across, as photo2.png shows it — a real team badge, not a printed graphic across the front. That position is a settled decision: do not centre it, do not enlarge it and do not add a second mark beside it. That position is settled and is the same in every frame.

IMAGE 2 SHOWS THIS ATHLETE WEARING THE REAL KIT. You are
photographing THOSE EXACT GARMENTS laid out flat and clean — not designing new
ones in the same colours, and not drawing what the words below describe.

WORK THROUGH THE GARMENT ELEMENT BY ELEMENT AND COPY EACH ONE EXACTLY AS THAT
PHOTOGRAPH SHOWS IT:
- the COLLAR: its shape, its colour, and whether it is laced or plain
- the SLEEVES: their length, and every band or stripe on them — HOW MANY there
  are, how wide each one is, and how far up the arm they sit
- the HEM and any waist band: its colour and its depth
- the BODY of the shirt: its colour, and any panel or piping, or none at all
- the CREST: its size, its shape, its colours and exactly where it sits
- the NUMBER: its colour, its outline, its shape, and every place it appears
- the shorts or pants, the socks and the footwear, the same way

Where the written list and that photograph disagree about how something LOOKS,
the PHOTOGRAPH IS RIGHT and the words are to be ignored. The list only decides
which items belong in the kit, which are branded, and what the photograph does
not show at all.

THE BADGE: take the artwork in image 1 and place it on the shirt UNCHANGED. Treat it as a finished graphic being applied to the garment, not as a subject to redraw or reinterpret: identical outline, identical figure inside, identical colours in identical places, identical proportions. Nothing added, nothing simplified, nothing restyled, and absolutely NO text — no club name, no letters, no word of any kind, not even small. POSITION: the badge sits SMALL ON THE LEFT CHEST, about a palm across, as photo2.png shows it — a real team badge, not a printed graphic across the front. That position is a settled decision: do not centre it, do not enlarge it and do not add a second mark beside it. Place it exactly there on the shirt as it lies facing you. SIZE: about one twelfth of the shirt's width. It is the ONLY graphic in the entire set.

Hard requirements:
- FULL-LENGTH GARMENTS ARE SHOWN AT FULL LENGTH: if the kit includes long trousers or
  pants, lay them out with BOTH legs extended completely straight, hems plainly visible
  at their full distance from the waistband — never folded under, never rolled, never
  cropped by another item, never arranged so they could be mistaken for knee-length.
  The poses copy the garment's LENGTH from this image, exactly like its colour.
- Everything is BRAND NEW and immaculate: no dirt, no scuffs, no creases beyond the fold
  of laying flat, no wear, no sweat marks. Copy what they wear, never its condition.
- Flat lay from directly overhead. No mannequin, no person, no body, no hanger, no rail.
- Plain light grey surface, evenly lit, soft shadows only. No props, no background objects.
- BRANDING follows the list above, item by item: an item described from the athlete's own photographs keeps the manufacturer's mark it really carries, and an item that came from the sport default is plain and unbranded. Never ADD a swoosh, three stripes, a cat, a jumpman, a trefoil or a wordmark to something the list did not say has one — these marks carry no letters, so "no text" does not cover them and they have to be refused by name.
- No words anywhere: no club name, no player name, no sponsor, no lettering, no woven
  neck label, no care label, no watermark. The squad number appears ONLY if the kit
  description above calls for it, and no other number is invented.
NO REAL-WORLD LEAGUE OR CLUB MARKS, ANYWHERE, EVER. No NFL shield, no NBA, no MLB, no NHL,
no FIFA, no UEFA, no Premier League, no NCAA, no Olympic rings, no national federation
badge, no professional club's crest — not on a jersey, a helmet, a sleeve, a collar, a
label, a ball or a boot, not even small and not even partly hidden. The only badge that
may appear anywhere is the club crest supplied with this request. These emblems carry no
letters, so "no text" does not cover them and they have to be refused by name.
- Sharp throughout, photographic, print quality. Square image.
